stem:
Meera's mother places a piece of solid ghee in a pan and heats it gently. The ghee becomes a liquid.

Which statement best explains why the ghee melts, and how its melting point is identified?

options.text: Heating makes the particles vibrate more strongly until they can leave their fixed positions; the melting point is the lowest temperature, at atmospheric pressure, at which the solid ghee becomes a liquid.
Heating makes the particles stop vibrating so they can flow; the melting point is the temperature at which the liquid ghee begins to boil.
Heating creates new particles that fill the gaps; the melting point is any temperature listed for ghee in a table of data.
Heating makes the particles larger so they push apart; the melting point is the highest temperature the solid ghee can reach before burning.

teacher.key_rationale: Melting occurs because added heat increases particle vibrations until particles escape their fixed positions in the solid lattice; the melting point is defined as the minimum temperature at which the solid becomes liquid at atmospheric pressure. Option A states both correctly. B reverses the vibration relationship and confuses melting with boiling, C invents new particles and treats the melting point as arbitrary table data, D wrongly claims particles grow in size.
